findings.reason: the stated mechanism is not the one producing the symptom, so the section would send a node to widen a lookup that already succeeds while the real cause (a missing catalogue in the reload image) is left in place.
findings.text: §63's Why says the alias `dsv4.1-flash` "is not found by that lookup, so it is cut to ten", but the alias IS declared at the backend top level (the model catalogue `docs/state/reckon/model-catalogue.yaml:47-50` sets `backends.clive.alias`), and `declared_model_aliases` reads exactly that key, so on the stated code path the cell is already 12 wide and `dsv4.1-flash` already fits; the observed ten-column cut comes from the pane's follower running in a reload tree that carries only `reckon/` and `skills/` (verified: `/home/ITER/mcintos/.config/reckon/crew/reload-trees/4695b8e9e67d6131/fa38bebd…` has no `docs/`), so the catalogue file is absent and no clive alias is read at all — a whole-layer absence the described per-model widening cannot repair

findings.reason: a done-when whose first case is green before the change cannot show the change did anything, and the node would close on a test that never fails for the defect it names.
findings.text: §63's first case ("renders rows whose agent alias is `dsv4.1-flash` at a 180-column pane and finds the alias in full") passes on the unfixed tree, because `declared_model_aliases(None)` already returns `('dsv4.1-flash', 'harness', 'sol6', 'sonnet 5.5')` and `model_cell_width` already returns 12, so the gate measures nothing about the change

findings.reason: the fix as written ("take the model the resolved backend's configuration launches with") already is the behaviour, so the section would deliver a no-op unless it names the real cause.
findings.text: §64's Why says "a dispatch the picker does not route records no model", but a fallback dispatch does record it: three live pointers with `picker_selection.action = "fallback"` carry a full agent record (`live/r-20261019T035327482346-ssog-anchor-family-runner.json` → `{'backend': 'clive', 'model': 'deepseek-v4.1-flash', 'alias': 'dsv4.1-flash'}`, and two codex fallbacks → `gpt-6-sol`/`sol6`), because `_agent_configuration` and `_stamp_agent_display` take model and alias from the resolved backend, which the model catalogue supplies; the cited `{'backend': 'clive', 'model': None}` is therefore not the picker fallback but a process whose backend config carried no model, i.e. again a reload-tree process with no catalogue

findings.reason: the negative control ("removes the fallback resolution") does not make the positive case fail, so the pair cannot distinguish fixed from unfixed and the node cannot prove it changed anything.
findings.text: §64's first case ("dispatches … a node whose picker selection is a fallback onto a backend that declares a model and an alias … finds the pointer's `agent.model` and `agent.alias` equal to the declared ones") already holds on the unfixed tree, as the live fallback pointers above show, so the node's gate passes before any change
